roundBegin.say: You, fresh off the shore. Every counter here has something for you.

roundWeaponsmith.say: Blades, shields and bows. A plain one always costs little here.
Better pieces come and go with the day.

roundArmorsmith.say: Head, body, arms and legs. I fit all four.
Start plain. Plain is what you can afford.

roundMage.say: Bring me Vestiges from the sea. I open them and say what they hold.

roundVault.say: What you leave with me stays here until you come back for it.

roundTailor.say: Dyes for your cloth and emblems for your back. Wear your colours well.

roundTack.say: Horses, and barding to dress them in. A good mount spares your legs.

roundMail.say: Letters for you wait here until you take them.

roundHarbour.say: The Shipwright's modules are sold here, to fit out your ship.
Keep your ship sound and it brings you home.

houseBegin.say: Hear all three houses before you choose. Start with the loudest.

houseStorm.say: Arlo Kestrel. We keep the Storm, and the Storm keeps nobody waiting.
You have met one of its hounds, I think. Pledge here and climb.

houseLamp.say: We mend what the sea breaks, and we keep the lamps lit.
Pledge with us and you will walk the Moors, where ships are lost.

houseVeil.say: Sable. That is all the name you will get.
We read what the Tithe writes. Pledge here and you read it too.

stormBegin.say: The Tithe took our storm-glass from the Old Beacon. Pell went after it.
Climb to the Old Beacon on the Downs. I will speak on the wind.

stormBeacon.say: Empty racks and Pell's knife. The Tithe carried the glass down to their barns.

stormCamp.say: Search the barns for the glass. Gather Brineglass too. It holds a storm.

stormGlass.say: That is our glass. Now climb as high as you can.

stormHold.say: Plant it on the High Downs and hold it. The Tithe will come.

stormLost.say: The glass is broken. Plant it again, and hold it this time.

stormCalled.say: Hold the glass up. Let the storm find you. There.
The Storm is yours now, and it will answer when you call.

stormTrail.say: Arlo? It is done. Do not come looking for me.
That was Pell. And Grey Point Light on the Moors burns with lightning.

stormQuicken.say: Pell's tracks run beside Tithe boots, toward their camp. You need quicker feet.
Let the storm into your legs. We call it Quicken.

stormLedger.say: No Pell. But their tally names a ship carrying our lightning rods to sea.

stormSea.say: Take a ship west. Find a Tithe sail and beat it.

stormIsle.say: Their crew talked. The rods went ashore on an isle they guard.

stormRods.say: Half our rods, in Tithe cloth. Take one, and shape the storm your way.

stormRiders.say: The rest rode up the Vale's river road with Pell. Run under my storm.

stormSlow.say: My storm has blown out. Back to Weir Mill, and I will call another.

stormPell.say: I lit Grey Point for them. They said it would pay my family's tenth.
Corvane is counting the storm. He means to sell it back to us.
Come home, Pell. And you, take this. We call it Arc Lash.

stormGround.say: They staked rods round the Old Stones to pull the storm down for him.
Strike them as the storm walks in: west, then north, east, and south.

stormWrong.say: No. West, then north, east, and south. Start again from the sea.

stormGrounded.say: The rods are cold. Corvane has nothing left to count.

stormMaw.say: The High Assessor waits in the Maw of the Shallows. End his counting.

stormFalls.say: Everything is owed. Even the storm. Even me.

stormCorvane.say: Not anymore. Bring the storm home.

stormHome.say: The racks are full again. Pell is mending them himself.
You climbed before you walked. That is a Stormcaller.
Thank you. I will not sell the sky again.

lampBegin.say: Someone stole our Beacon's lens. Its light reaches half as far now.
A ship broke at Shingle Landing. Go. Our lamps will carry my voice.

lampShingle.say: Are you real? There were lights ashore. We steered for them. Then rocks.
False lights, where our Beacon should have shone. Keep that boy safe.

lampFold.say: Ewe Fold will take him in. Walk him there, and keep him close.

lampWalk.say: Stay near me. Whoever lit those lights is still out there.

lampBarrows.say: Those barrows are where the false lights burn. Keep him moving.

lampSafe.say: They were waiting for us to break. I heard them laughing.
He is safe. Now go back and put out every false light.

lampSunwell.say: Dark again. Their purses hold Tithe silver, paid out at Gullwing in the Vale.
Hang a sun where you stand. All near it heal. That is the Sunwell.

lampMend.say: The Tithe beat Gullwing for seeing them pay wreckers. They will come back.
The light can close your own wounds now. We call it Mend.

lampLost.say: They reached the wounded. Go back, and hold them this time.

lampPay.say: The wreckers' ship waits offshore for its pay. Sail west and find it.

lampCove.say: Their captain spoke of a cove. Whatever they took is buried there.

lampLens.say: Their hoard, but not our lens. Choose what the light becomes in your hands.

lampHulks.say: Their tally says it was sold at the Saltbreaker Hulks, on the Moors.

lampBuyer.say: Lamplighters. The Tithe bought your lens fair. Go home.

lampDawn.say: Nothing stolen is bought fair. Burn their dark away. That is Dawnflare.

lampGrey.say: Grey Point burns for the Tithe. Set it true: red, white, green, then gold.

lampWrong.say: Not that one. Red, then white, then green, then gold.

lampLit.say: Grey Point burns true, and its light finds the Pearl Tomb's door.

lampTomb.say: The Reeve answered to someone in the Tomb. Our lens is there. End it.

lampFalls.say: The Tithe will light its own lamps.

lampReeve.say: Then they will burn without us. Bring the lens home.

lampHome.say: The lens is back on the Beacon. Every ship at sea will see it.
Tobin watched it light from Ewe Fold. You light the way now.

veilBegin.say: The Tithe wrote your name in their book before you washed ashore.
I want that page. Their collectors carry tallies through Saltgrass. Follow one.

veilTail.say: There. That collector. Keep him in sight, and never close.

veilNoticed.say: He felt you there. Let him settle, then try again.

veilRuin.say: He left his tallies in the ruin. Lift every one before he comes back.

veilTallies.say: Your name on every tally, and a sum. The book is close.

veilAdit.say: Its reckoner works in the Chalk Adit. Get there with no eye on you.

veilSeen.say: They saw you. Get clear, and try again.

veilRaven.say: You came unseen. Good. The reckoner has gone to Moorhold, on the Moors.
Take the dark with you. Its raven wounds them, and heals you.

veilDaggers.say: His guards hold Moorhold, too many to walk past. So do not walk.
Throw. We call them Dusk Daggers.

veilShip.say: The reckoner put to sea with the book, aboard a Tithe ship.

veilSea.say: Sail west and take a Tithe ship's deck. Search it for the book.

veilIsle.say: No book aboard, but their log names the reckoner's isle.

veilLedger.say: No book here. Only his ledger, in a cipher Wren can read.
Choose what the dark becomes in your hands. Wren waits at Vale Mouth.

veilWren.say: You are the one Thule could not drown. Keep up, and keep quiet.

veilOrchard.say: Collectors work this orchard. Heads down. We are only walking.

veilHalf.say: His ledger says half your debt is paid already. By someone in Overlook.
Interesting. Vanish now, and follow the book. Like this.

veilMarks.say: The ledger puts his chest at Valeguard. It opens by four marks.
Touch them as he counts: tithe, debt, interest, then fee.

veilWrong.say: Wrong. Tithe, then debt, then interest, then fee. He counts the tithe first.

veilOpened.say: Empty, but for a slip in his hand. One word: Grotto.

veilGrotto.say: Kraken's Grotto, then. The book went down there, and its keeper never leaves.

veilKeeper.say: Your name stays written. The book remembers.

veilBook.say: The book. Your name is in it. I have read no further.

veilHome.say: I burned your page unread. The Tithe will have to remember you unwritten.
Who paid half? That question keeps.
We never say welcome. You will know it anyway.
